Fact.Name: Social Security (OASDI) wage base TY2026
Fact.Description: TY2026 OASDI contribution and benefit base = $184,500. Primary source: SSA https://www.ssa.gov/oact/cola/cbb.html ("For earnings in 2026, this base is $184,500.") Also: 90 Fed. Reg. (Nov. 3, 2025) announcing $184,500 for remuneration paid in 2026 and self-employment income earned in tax years beginning in 2026.

Fact.Name: SE tax filing threshold
Fact.Description: Net earnings from self-employment of $400 or more generally require Schedule SE / SE tax. Cite: 26 U.S.C. § 1402; Schedule SE instructions.

Fact.Name: Net profit subject to SE tax before 92.35%
Fact.Description: Positive Schedule C net profit subject to SE tax (MVP: no farm/optional methods). Cite: 26 U.S.C. § 1402(a); Schedule SE.

Fact.Name: Net earnings from self-employment
Fact.Description: Schedule SE: net profit × 92.35% (0.9235). Cite: Schedule SE instructions (multiply by 92.35%); reflects employer-equivalent portion already excluded via the 7.65% reduction embedded in 92.35% (= 100% − 7.65%). Related: 26 U.S.C. § 1402(a)(12) / Schedule SE computational worksheet. Rational 9235/10000 = 0.9235.

Fact.Name: SE tax applies
Fact.Description: True when net earnings from SE ≥ $400. Cite: Schedule SE; 26 U.S.C. § 1402.

Fact.Name: Primary filer total OASDI wages (W-2 Box 3)
Fact.Description: Sum of primary filer W-2 social security wages for Schedule SE wage-base coordination. Cite: Schedule SE — Social Security wages reduce remaining wage base for the 12.4% portion.

Fact.Name: Remaining Social Security wage base for SE
Fact.Description: max(0, TY2026 wage base $184,500 − W-2 OASDI wages). Cite: SSA CBB https://www.ssa.gov/oact/cola/cbb.html ; Schedule SE Part I lines for "Social security wages and tips".

Fact.Name: SE earnings subject to 12.4% Social Security tax
Fact.Description: Lesser of net earnings from SE and remaining Social Security wage base. Rate authority: 26 U.S.C. § 1401(a) — 12.4% on self-employment income. Quote (§ 1401(a)): "a tax equal to 12.4 percent of the amount of the self-employment income…" https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/1401

Fact.Name: Social Security portion of SE tax
Fact.Description: 12.4% × SE Social Security taxable earnings. Cite: 26 U.S.C. § 1401(a). Rational 124/1000 = 0.124.

Fact.Name: SE earnings subject to 2.9% Medicare tax
Fact.Description: Net earnings from SE when SE tax applies (no wage base for HI after 1993). Cite: 26 U.S.C. § 1401(b); SSA note that HI has no limitation after 1993.

Fact.Name: Medicare (HI) portion of SE tax
Fact.Description: 2.9% × SE Medicare taxable earnings. Cite: 26 U.S.C. § 1401(b). Rational 29/1000 = 0.029. Note: Additional 0.9% Medicare tax above threshold is OUT OF SCOPE in this slice (explicit).

Fact.Name: Self-employment tax
Fact.Description: Total SE tax = Social Security portion + Medicare portion. Schedule SE → Schedule 2 (other taxes) → Form 1040. Cite: 26 U.S.C. § 1401; Schedule SE instructions.

Fact.Name: Deductible part of self-employment tax
Fact.Description: Employer-equivalent portion = one-half of SE tax. Schedule 1 adjustment. Cite: 26 U.S.C. § 164(f) — https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/164#f Quote: deduction equal to the employer-equivalent portion of the taxes imposed by section 1401.

Fact.Name: Schedule C section complete
Fact.Description: Interview complete for Schedule C MVP (or filer had no SE income).
